$comment: The TypeScript compiler, pinned. This is not a Node project - nothing here
is published, imported or shipped, and no engine code is JavaScript. The
file exists so that `just typecheck` runs a compiler this repository chose
rather than whichever one was newest that morning.
It pinned nothing before: the recipe ran `bunx tsc`, which resolves to the
`latest` tag and fetches it. A compiler upgrade could therefore change what
the check accepts with no commit anywhere - the exact failure mode
docs/DEFERRED.md records for `just docs-check`, where a check nobody could
reproduce stopped being true while still claiming to pass.
**Exact, with no caret, and there is no lockfile on purpose.** TypeScript 7
is the native compiler: its dependencies are one prebuilt binary per
platform and upstream pins every one of them to its own exact version. So
`7.0.2` already names the whole tree, and a lockfile would add nothing
except a format to disagree about - bun writes `bun.lock`, npm writes
`package-lock.json`, and the Justfile accepts either runner.
Bump it deliberately: change the version, run `just typecheck`, and review
what the new compiler says. `mono.engine/script/bindings/engine.d.ts` is
generated, so a diagnostic that appears here is either a real disagreement
or a change in the compiler worth knowing about.
name: atomic-game-engine-scripts
